name: Yahoo

Software Engineer.dsaDepth: Light–Moderate - process length and depth vary enormously by report, from a lightweight 2-round loop to a full 4-round onsite with system design, database design and two algorithm problems
rounds: Simpler pipelines (some 2025-26 reports): an online coding round on your core tech stack, then a single hiring-manager interview covering technical depth and project discussion

Fuller pipelines (older/some current reports): phone screen, then a 4-round onsite (4-5 hours) covering 1 system design question, 1 database-design question, and 2 algorithm problems (e.g. binary tree search, a Twitter-style newsfeed schema design, Two Sum)
Campus pipelines: a single onsite session with 2 problems in 45 minutes (OOP design plus a coding problem) and a brief Q&A
extraTopics: Explaining your approach and depth of understanding of the underlying system/website architecture, not just producing a correct answer - interviewers are reported to actively guide candidates toward the right direction
Adapting to a genuinely wide range of process lengths and depths - treat any single report as one data point, not the process
Software Engineer.notes: Multiple recent reports mention scheduling issues (a hiring manager not showing up) and reduced structure compared to the fuller historical loop - the process appears to have become less consistent in recent years.

rolesNotes: The wide variance in process length and depth across independent reports is itself the most consistent finding - Yahoo’s process appears to lack the standardization seen at most other companies in this batch, and several recent reports mention scheduling/organizational issues.
